newsitem.title: GERMANY: FedEx starts five weekly Par-Mos freighter.
newsitem.headline: FedEx starts five weekly Par-Mos freighter.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said it had added Moscow to its global air cargo network with the start of a five days a week freighter service from Paris Tuesday.
The freight integrator said it will fly a Boeing 727-200 with 25 tonnes freight capacity from Paris via Frankfurt to Moscow Vnukovo airport with a return flight via Munich to Paris.

FedEx managing director Germany, Antje Schuett, said at a news conference in Frankfurt: "We are the first freight airline to fly to Moscow with our own freighter. Up to now, we consolidated on other airlines."
"The flight means the end of the 32kg express shipment barrier and the opportunity to send dangerous goods," she added.

FedEx would now be able to send shipments of up to 682kg and planned a dangerous goods service as soon as possible since this was a major client wish, especially from the chemical industry, Schuett said.

The new Russia service offered guaranteed distribution times, door-to-door delivery, full customs clearance in-house and a money-back guarantee for late deliveries covering both directions, she added.
"To Moscow we have a two-day ex-U.S. service and 24-hour service from western Europe, and from Moscow, we will link western Europe with a 24-hour service and the U.S. overnight," she said.
Within Russia and ex-Soviet republics, the airline is offering 24-48 hour deliveries using local carriers from Moscow, she added.

FedEx has opened its own warehouse with Russian customs clearance facilities and officials at Vnukovo airport while Russian courier service Elf will carry out Moscow distribution in vans carrying the FedEx logo, Schuett said.
